originalTitle: Trump’s Air Force One deception faces scrutiny over ‘decoy’ passengers
summary: Journalists and others were allowed to fly on presidential jet despite security threat while Trump was spirited away
content: Democrats called on Tuesday for a congressional briefing over a stunning charade in which Donald Trump was secretly spirited to different plane than the one the public and press believed he was travelling on. Critics now question why reporters and the public had been deliberately misled. When US intelligence allegedly found a credible threat that Iran plotted to kill him last month, Trump left Air Force One in a catering truck, an episode first reported by the Washington Post and also by the New York Times. While the president was reportedly snuck out the side door of the plane, more than a hundred aides, officials and reporters were kept onboard to fly towards Britain, without being told there was a threat to their lives. “It appears that the idea was we can reduce the danger to President Trump by offering up 100 or so people to be killed by the Iranians in his place,” said Steven Cash, executive director of the Steady State and a former CIA intelligence officer and senior adviser to the Department of Homeland Security’s intelligence branch. Richard Blumenthal, a Democratic senator for Connecticut, called the operation “unprecedented and surreal” and “downright scary” on CNN. “There has to be a congressional briefing because it involves not just the safety of the president. “I want to know what precautions were taken to make sure that all of the passengers on that Air Force One, which was judged too dangerous for the president to fly on, what precautions were taken to keep the staff and reporters on that plane safe?” The White House had publicly said the president would fly to Britain onboard Air Force One – albeit an older version instead of the new Qatari-gifted aircraft. In reality, Trump boarded the presidential jet in full view of television cameras before being spirited away minutes later and transferred to an air force C-32A. The deception was sufficiently elaborate that journalists travelling with the president – and some White House staff – believed Trump remained onboard Air Force One. Reporters were instructed to keep the shades over their windows closed during the flight. The C-32A carrying Trump flew to RAF Mildenhall in Britain, arriving at about 10.20pm. The older Air Force One and the travelling press pool arrived minutes later. Photographers subsequently captured Trump descending from the presidential aircraft, apparently after he had been secretly reunited with it. Trump then greeted troops at the base before boarding the newly refurbished Boeing 747 donated by Qatar and flying on to Washington. Ned Price, a former deputy to the US ambassador to the UN, said he did not begrudge any White House taking extraordinary measures to protect the president but the current administration had perpetuated an “outright lie” for weeks and turned reporters into “unwitting conspirators”. Price, an ex-special assistant to President Barack Obama on the national security council, added: “There was a way to do this where they didn’t need to lie. They could have enlisted the travelling press pool, who would have very willingly, I am certain, not reported on certain security arrangements. “Once all was said and done and the president was safely in the UK or back at Andrews air force base, they could have said, ‘This is what we did and this is why we did it,’” Price added. “But they feel no compunction to the truth. They feel no loyalty to the truth. Instead it’s just an effort over the past month to lie and to mislead.” Journalists also raised concerns. Jake Tapper, an anchor on CNN, tweeted: “Obviously the life of the president is paramount, and previous White Houses have used deception to protect the president’s life. But no officials I’ve spoken to have ever before heard of using an AF1 full of WH staff and journalists as a decoy during an imminent threat.” The White House has not directly confirmed the details of the operation. Its communications director, Steven Cheung, instead told the Post the president faced numerous threats and that officials used “every tool at our disposal” to protect him. The revelation sheds new light on an abrupt decision that had already raised questions about the security of the Qatari aircraft. Trump had flown the newly refurbished jet to the Nato summit – its first international journey – but unexpectedly announced that he would instead use the older Air Force One on the first leg of his return journey. At the time, Trump said the new aircraft was being flown to Mildenhall so US troops stationed there could inspect it. The New York Times and CBS News subsequently reported that intelligence officials had raised concerns about a possible attack on Trump or his aircraft amid the escalating conflict with Iran. During the summit, the US military was conducting major strikes against Iran, adding to fears of Iranian retaliation. The new account suggests that the threat was taken more seriously than previously understood. Not everyone is convinced the threat justified what happened next. “From the Iranian perspective, pulling off an attempted targeting of presidential aircraft at this depth would be extremely implausible; it would require close-in clandestine operators with man-portable anti-air systems,” said Ankit Panda, the Stanton senior fellow in the nuclear policy program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Panda said it was not clear there had been a specific, credible threat within Turkey itself, though presidential security routinely plans around “known unknowns”. “Iran doesn’t have surface-to-air missiles that could target an aircraft taking off from Ankara,” said Dr Jeffrey Lewis, a distinguished fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute. Iran could in theory strike a plane on the runway with a ballistic missile, he said, “but that seems very unlikely”. chineseTitle: 特朗普的空军一号欺骗行为面临“诱骗”乘客的审查
chineseSummary: 尽管存在安全威胁，但特朗普被偷偷带走时，记者和其他人仍被允许乘坐总统专机
chineseContent: 周二，民主党人呼吁就一场令人震惊的猜谜游戏举行简报会，在这场猜谜游戏中，唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)秘密乘坐的飞机与公众和媒体认为他乘坐的飞机不同。批评者现在质疑为什么记者和公众被故意误导。当美国情报部门据称发现伊朗上个月密谋杀害他的可信威胁时，特朗普将空军一号留在了一辆餐饮卡车上，这一事件首先由《华盛顿邮报》和《纽约时报》报道。据报道，总统从飞机侧门溜了出来，但一百多名助手、官员和记者仍留在飞机上，准备飞往英国，但没有被告知他们的生命受到威胁。 “我们的想法似乎是，我们可以通过提供 100 名左右的人来代替特朗普总统被伊朗人杀害，从而减少对特朗普总统的危险，”稳定国家组织执行董事、前中央情报局情报官员、国土安全部情报部门高级顾问史蒂文·卡什 (Steven Cash) 说。康涅狄格州民主党参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔 (Richard Blumenthal) 在 CNN 上称这次行动“史无前例、超现实”和“彻头彻尾的可怕”。 “必须向国会通报情况，因为这不仅仅涉及总统的安全。我想知道采取了哪些预防措施来确保这架空军一号上的所有乘客，这架飞机被认为对总统来说太危险而不能乘坐，采取了哪些预防措施来保证飞机上工作人员和记者的安全？”白宫曾公开表示，总统将乘坐空军一号飞往英国——尽管是旧型号，而不是卡塔尔赠送的新型飞机。事实上，特朗普在电视摄像机的众目睽睽之下登上了总统专机，然后才被逮捕。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
